state.misconception_label: Does not understand that 2n represents an even number

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: Which of these shows part of the proof that the sum of two odd numbers is even? I got \( \begin{array}{l}2 n+(2 m+1) \\ =2(n+m)+1\end{array} \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You are correct in starting with \(2n+(2m+1)\), but remember that 2n represents an even number. Therefore, the sum of two odd numbers will result in an even number. Make sure to consider the properties of even and odd numbers when simplifying expressions.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get that \(2n\) is an even number, but I’m still confused about how that helps with adding the odd number \(2m + 1\). So, if I add an even number to an odd number, how does that make it even? Can you explain that part again?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: When adding an even number to an odd number, the result will always be an odd number. Remember that odd + even = odd. So in the expression \(2n+(2m+1)\), the sum will be an odd number. Keep this in mind when simplifying the expression.
